prompts.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit
Asset type: architectural concept board for a Korean first-person writing cafe. This is a proposal only, not an actual app screenshot.
Reference images:
1) Actual garden-to-cafe screenshot: authoritative existing connected room layout, glazing, communal table, bookshelves and material positions.
2) Actual garden entry screenshot: authoritative modest garden layout with two small trees, low flowers, goldfish pond, outdoor bench and writing table.
3) Previously approved after-work concept: material and brand reference only. Its lighting is TOO DARK for this new request; make the new proposal visibly brighter.
Primary request: the user specifically says the GARDEN ↔ CAFE GLASS DOOR and approach look too narrow, and the lighting may be too dark. Show a clear, convincing wider passage with brighter warm-white light. Do NOT redesign the main street entrance or the quiet alcove arch.

Produce ONE landscape design board with TWO equally large first-person perspective panels of THE SAME widened garden/cafe door, readable as one spatially continuous place:
Left label exactly "정원에서 카페로"
Right label exactly "카페에서 정원으로"
Small board title exactly "넓은 유리문 · 밝은 원목 카페"
Small status exactly "시안 · 앱 미반영"
Small bottom specification exactly "문 폭 약 1.8m · 문 앞 여유 약 1.5m — 설계 목표"
Typography: restrained dark brown Korean type on warm ivory margins. Each view must have substantial screen space, no tiny triptych, no fake app HUD, no floating action buttons.

Door and circulation proposal:
The door remains at the existing rear end of the window wall joining the garden to the cafe. Replace the narrow roughly 1m passage with a full-height approximately 1.8m-wide CLEAR opening in the warm walnut glazed facade. Use a single broad wood-framed sliding glass leaf parked to ONE SIDE over adjacent fixed glazing, so that the entire 1.8m opening is visibly EMPTY; no central mullion or fixed glass masquerading as a passage. Show the parked glass leaf and its simple recessed upper track and brass pull so the door operation is understandable. The leaf must not swing into the path or beyond the garden boundary wall. Keep the threshold flush, the mocha interior stone transitioning to a broad light stone landing in the garden. Pull the nearest rear window desk a little away along the window wall and move the garden bench/table slightly farther from the door to leave an obvious approximately 1.5m-deep clear approach on both sides. No chair backs, planters, stepping-stone bottlenecks or narrow wood posts in the approach. Camera eye-height approximately 1.62m, normal human perspective, no ultra-wide lens trick to fake width. Convey width relative to the familiar human-scale chairs and tables without adding people.

Lighting:
Noticeably brighter than both the actual cafe and the previously dark proposal. Warm-white pendants and wall lights with broad soft ambient bounce; ivory plaster, wood grain, ceiling edges and the entire walkable floor are readily visible. Writing paper remains bright and comfortable to read. A warm and welcoming early-evening room with gentle daylight still in the garden; avoid dark amber, brown haze, black corners, theatrical spot pools, overexposed windows and glaring bulbs. Keep relaxed warmth while increasing useful room brightness. No global dark vignette.

Preserve:
Same mid-size cafe; large six-person central oak table, walnut chairs/frames and right-side shelving, back coffee counter and existing quiet writing alcove, ivory plaster and mocha matte stone floor. Keep the communal table and its clear aisles. Modest connected garden of two small trees, restrained low planting and the same small goldfish pond off to the side, NOT in the walking path. Both panels must depict the same door width, frame, threshold, parked leaf and garden/cafe relation, not two different doors. The pond need not appear centered through the door; it can remain sideways through adjoining windows. Same building boundary and floor levels. Do not add a new lobby, corridor extension, gatehouse, extra rooms, luxury finishes, dense forest, new furniture, avatars, people or shopping area.

Rendering:
Clean warm stylized architectural 3D concept, retain recognizable existing cafe furniture shapes, detailed enough to judge doorway clearance and increased brightness; do not claim this is a captured runtime image. The view from the garden MUST show an unobstructed route through the doorway into the actual cafe, and the view from inside MUST show the matching landing and modest garden.
